<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These <strong>oven baked pork chops</strong> are the most popular baked pork chop recipe on the internet for good reason: they’re easy to make, tender, super juicy, and flavorful. A few simple ingredients and pantry-staple spices are all you need to make this incredible dinner.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="1456" height="2184" data-pin-title="Baked Pork Chops" src="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops.jpg" alt="An oven baked pork chop on a dinner plate with mashed potatoes and peas." class="wp-image-106214" srcset="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops.jpg 1456w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-750x1125.jpg 750w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-330x495.jpg 330w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-680x1020.jpg 680w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-1365x2048.jpg 1365w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-40x60.jpg 40w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-730x1095.jpg 730w, https://www.theendlessmeal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Baked-Pork-Chops-150x225.jpg 150w" sizes="(min-width: 1200px) 730px, (min-width: 1080px) 650px, (min-width: 1024px) 630px, calc(100vw - 40px)"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Get ready for truly tender and juicy pork chops! Baking them in a small dish in the oven prevents them from drying out. It’s an easy method that always delivers great results.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Not to brag, but I’ve been told I’m <a href="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/recipes/ingredient/pork/pork-chops/">an expert at making pork chops</a>. I reach for them often as they’re inexpensive and quick to cook. This meal is one of my family’s favorite <a href="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/recipes/dinner/">dinner recipes</a>, and we return to it often. The flavorful pork chops always turn out tender and juicy. After you make these baked pork chops, you’ll make them again and again. The recipe is speedy and easy to prepare and is a great one to keep in your back pocket for when you need dinner stat or can’t figure out what to make tonight. You can use boneless or bone-in pork chops – it’s your choice!</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In this recipe, I keep it simple and don’t sear the chops on the stove. Instead, they go straight into the oven. In my experience, this makes the chops more tender and saves an extra step. And with the gorgeous color of the spices, you won’t miss the sear. Serve these with a big salad and some potatoes roasted in the oven at the same time as the pork chops. It makes for the best dinner.</p>



<p class="has-gray-light-background-color has-background wp-block-paragraph">Try these <a href="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/smothered-pork-chops/">smothered pork chops</a> and <a href="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/pan-fried-pork-chops/">pan-fried pork chops</a> next. Or go for my popular <a href="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/baked-pork-tenderloin/">baked pork tenderloin</a>!</p>

<h2 id="h-how-long-do-pork-chops-take-to-bake-at-400-degrees" class="wp-block-heading has-gray-background-color has-background"><span id="How_long_do_pork_chops_take_to_bake_at_400_degrees">How long do pork chops take to bake at 400 degrees?</span></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Overcooking is the number one reason pork chops turn out dry, and the fix is simple: bake boneless pork chops for 7 minutes per half inch of thickness at 400 degrees Fahrenheit, and bone-in chops for 8 minutes per half inch.</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>Bake boneless pork chops 1 ½ inches thick for 21 minutes.</strong></li>



<li><strong>Bake bone-in pork chops 1 ½ inches thick for 24 minutes.</strong></li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The most reliable way to check doneness is an instant-read thermometer: pull them at 145°F and let them rest for 5 minutes in the pan before serving.</p>

<h2 id="h-store-and-reheat" class="wp-block-heading has-gray-background-color has-background"><span id="Store_and_Reheat">Store and Reheat</span></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Store:</strong> I love a good pork chop sliced over a salad for lunch, so I sometimes make extra for leftovers. They will keep for 3-4 days in a covered container in your fridge.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Reheat: </strong>I like to slice them thin and warm them briefly in a pan over medium heat. You can also use a microwave.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Freeze: </strong>Yes! If you’d like to meal prep, these baked pork chops will keep for at least 3 months in the freezer.</p>

		<div id="recipe-58630-notes" class="wprm-recipe-notes-container wprm-block-text-normal"><h3 class="wprm-recipe-header wprm-recipe-notes-header wprm-block-text-normal wprm-align-left wprm-header-decoration-none" style="">Notes</h3><div class="wprm-recipe-notes"><span style="display: block;"><strong>This recipe works best with pork chops at least 1 inch thick.</strong> For thin pork chops, I recommend using my <a href="https://www.theendlessmeal.com/how-to-cook-thin-pork-chops/">thin pork chops recipe</a>.</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span class="block-editor-rich-text__editable schema-faq-question rich-text" role="textbox" contenteditable="true" aria-multiline="true" aria-label="Enter a question" data-wp-block-attribute-key="faq-question-1709575452892-question" style="display: block;"><strong>What cuts of pork should I use to make this recipe?</strong> I love using rib chops, but pork loin chops and center-cut chops also work great. If the pork chops you buy don’t indicate what type they are, don’t worry! This recipe works great with all chops that are at least 1 inch thick.</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>Baking time:</strong> Bake your boneless pork chops for 7 minutes per ½ inch of thickness, and bake bone-in pork chops for 8 minutes per half inch.</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>Baking dish: </strong>Choose a baking dish that is just the right size for the pork chops. There shouldn’t be too much room between them, or the juices will evaporate in the oven. If you don’t have the right-sized baking dish, use a cast-iron or ovenproof frying pan instead. </span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><b>Elevation: </b>This recipe has been tested at sea level. As elevation affects cooking time, you may need to cook your pork chops a little longer if you live at a higher elevation. </span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>Spice blend:</strong> You can switch up the spices in this recipe. If you have a seasoning blend you love, go ahead and use it!</span></div></div>
